clue.text: Points which make for a dilemma

definitions.meaning: sharp pointed growths on an animal's head, such as a bull's
a dilemma is pictured as a bull with two of these, either of which may gore you

explanation.definitionFit: Points are the sharp tips on a bull's head, and the idiom 'on the horns of a dilemma' means caught between two bad choices.

clue.text: The line for a horticulturalist to take?

definitions.text: The line for a horticulturalist to take?

parts.words: The line for a horticulturalist to take?
parts.note: a 'line to take' usually means a policy or argument, but here the line is a literal flexible tube a gardener drags across the lawn

explanation.surface: A question about what policy a gardener should adopt.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's watering tube is a long line carried round the garden.

clue.text: A dish to stir nothing to it

annotationWithheld.why: A dish to stir nothing to it (7): RISOTTO is an anagram of TO STIR plus O, but 'stir' must be both the anagram fodder and its only indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: A dish to stir nothing to it

clue.text: Locate a bridge in mass panic

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words mass panic, across the word break

explanation.surface: An instruction to find a bridge amid crowd hysteria.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the stretch of a bridge between supports, and by extension a bridge itself.

clue.text: So heavenly a herb — a trifle sweet, maybe

parts.note: so heavenly is like an angel, angelic

explanation.surface: A heavenly herb that might be used to sweeten a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: The candied green stems of this plant are a traditional decoration on a British trifle, a layered custard-and-sponge pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is an aromatic plant whose candied stems decorate cakes and puddings.

clue.text: Stay on ship in Barrie's fantasy world

definitions.meaning: a sailor who stays aboard will, cryptically, not ever come ashore
J M Barrie's Peter Pan lives in this imaginary island

explanation.surface: Remaining aboard ship within the magical world of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as advice, the phrase means not ever going ashore; it is also the name of Peter Pan's imaginary island in J M Barrie's play.

clue.text: Take Latin and get on at school

parts.note: et is the Latin word for and
taken as written after the Latin word; that the letters also run across the words get on is a coincidence, as get is only a link here

explanation.surface: Advice to study Latin and do well at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'get' are just links. Eton is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school in Berkshire.

clue.text: Ian's twice taken right nationality

indicators.note: the doubled name takes in the extra letter
the name is written out two times in a row

parts.note: the man's name Ian, as written

explanation.surface: Ian has twice adopted the correct nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives IANIAN, and 'taken' puts R inside it after the first I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Iran has this nationality.

clue.text: So be it an old penny to change

parts.note: amen, said at the end of a prayer, means so be it
d was the abbreviation for a penny in British money before 1971, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: Agreeing to alter an old penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to revise or alter it.

clue.text: Oddly, police on trains in charge of children

indicators.note: done oddly, the letters are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: Police strangely riding trains while looking after children.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means acting in the place of a parent, as a teacher or guardian responsible for youngsters.

clue.text: Sanction leaves us in a spot

indicators.note: the word us is placed inside the word for a spot

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark
taken as written

explanation.surface: A penalty that leaves a blot on our record.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction a ruling is to uphold or confirm it, as a judge might.

clue.text: Sebastian's sister open to endless abuse

parts.note: Viola is Sebastian's twin sister in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

indicators.note: the openings of the words to and endless are their first letters

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean heroine laid bare to unending mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' looks like an adjective (exposed), but it signals the opening letters, T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate someone or something is to mistreat or desecrate it.

clue.text: Mine's full of holes

parts.note: a coal mine is a pit, and a surface pocked with small hollows has these too

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that their own item is riddled with holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Small holes or hollows are pits, and a colliery is also a pit.

clue.text: A worthless apology

explanation.definitionFit: A pitiful, wretched thing is described by this word, which is also the commonest spoken apology.

clue.text: Girl's prison sentence

definitions.meaning: British slang for a young woman, with 's standing for is
British slang for time in jail

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a young woman is called this, and doing time in jail is also called this, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time.

clue.text: Pinpoint localities

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning locates exactly, read as he or she pinpoints

explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice and locate it, and spots are also places.

clue.text: A charming accent

parts.note: cute means charming or sweet

explanation.surface: A delightful way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' means not a way of speaking but a mark written over a letter, as on the e in café.
explanation.definitionFit: The rising mark written over a vowel, as in café, is one kind of diacritical mark.

clue.text: Morning stare ' will trail shines in the dark

annotationWithheld.why: Morning stare ' will trail shines in the dark (14): the OCR text is garbled ('stare', a stray apostrophe); PHOSPHOR + E + SCENT seems intended but the clue words for E and SCENT cannot be read
annotationWithheld.clue: Morning stare ' will trail shines in the dark

clue.text: Ad about get-away to an adventure

indicators.note: the escape word goes around the ad

parts.note: a getaway is an escape
taken as written

explanation.surface: An advertisement promoting a holiday break as an adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous exploit.

clue.text: Infringements of art in accepted behaviour

annotationWithheld.why: Infringements of art in accepted behaviour (14): CONVENTIONS around TRA, but no clue word signals that ART is reversed or rearranged
annotationWithheld.clue: Infringements of art in accepted behaviour

clue.text: A violation going without changing gear

parts.note: without in its old sense of outside gives out

indicators.note: the letters of the word gear are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A breach of rules: driving without changing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges GEAR into RAGE; 'going' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shocking act that breaches decency.

clue.text: The total garment

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning complete or taken as a whole
a loose protective garment worn over clothes

explanation.definitionFit: An overall cost is the complete sum, and an overall is a protective coat or smock.

clue.text: Taking tome out, find speck of dust

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the book's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Removing a book from a shelf and spotting dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A mote is a tiny particle, as in the biblical mote in your brother's eye.

clue.text: How's the weather? I can see nothing in the mist

indicators.note: the letters for nothing and I are placed inside the mist

parts.note: taken as the plain word mist
O looks like the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone answers a weather question by saying they can see nothing in the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question whose answer is the solution: damp weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp, drizzly weather is described as wet in a light way.

clue.text: Quaker dessert recipe?

parts.note: Quaker suggests the religious Friends, but here it means something that quakes or wobbles on the plate

explanation.surface: A request for a pudding recipe from the Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A wobbly set pudding made with gelatine quakes when moved.

clue.text: Half true name of wartime singer

definitions.text: Half true name of wartime singer

parts.words: Half true name of wartime singer
parts.note: the Forces' Sweetheart of the Second World War was born ... Welch, so the first of her two real names is half of it

explanation.surface: A question about the real name of a famous wartime entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Vera Lynn sang 'We'll Meet Again' in the Second World War; her birth name was Vera Margaret Welch.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera Lynn, Britain's best-loved wartime singer, kept her first name from birth.

clue.text: Politician's chair?

parts.note: an MP wins a place in parliament, called by this name, as well as the furniture sat on

explanation.surface: A question about the furniture a politician sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of parliament holds a constituency place in the House, and a chair is something to sit on.

clue.text: Alcoholics about, about the neighbourhood

indicators.note: the first about says the AA goes around the next piece

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Drinkers hanging around the local streets.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or locality.

clue.text: I've simply no idea what to put here!

definitions.text: I've simply no idea what to put here!

parts.words: I've simply no idea what to put here!
parts.note: the exclamation of a stumped solver is also the phrase that fills the grid

explanation.surface: A baffled solver giving up on this very clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday phrase for being completely baffled says exactly what the clue exclaims.

clue.text: For pop group, it's sheer bliss

definitions.meaning: the American grunge band fronted by Kurt Cobain
the Buddhist state of perfect peace

explanation.definitionFit: It names Kurt Cobain's grunge band and the Buddhist state of perfect happiness and release.

clue.text: Composes essay, unusual satire on ET

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer composes an essay as an odd satire on the film alien ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a long formal written study of a subject.

clue.text: See 27
